For patients with hiatal hernia repair during laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding, having fewer sutures (anterior sutures) or no sutures at all may not significantly impact the OR time. However, there are no clear associations between the number of sutures placed and readmission rates, reoperations related to band-related issues, or postoperative weight loss.

In fact, the study suggests that technical aspects of HHR (hiatal hernia repair) do not appear to be associated with these outcomes, indicating that a standardized approach may not be necessary. This implies that whether fewer sutures are placed or if no sutures are used during the procedure does not seem to affect the overall quality of care or the likelihood of complications.

It's essential to note that while this study provides some insight into the topic, more research is needed to fully understand any potential benefits or drawbacks of using fewer sutures or no sutures in hiatal hernia repair.
